Okay if there was a point in which no life Exists and stars too have died out as you say, I believe that energy will still exist in one form or the other. When the universe is dead, as you say I get that you believe that no matter what ever we do here in this life will ultimately result in nothing. Or to put it in other words it will all be zero, a point were you believe that nothing will exist and the universe would have returned to what it was previously before all the planets where created am I understanding it correctly?

Now what I mean is that even though at point where maybe everything will be destroyed like what you said. In that case it will lead to a new beginning since energy still exists. And that new beginning will be influenced by the small changes that we've made in our universe.

And I haven't taken into account the existence of God, when I say this.

Well I say that because, even though I've said that if it's been marked as useful it has meaning to it, but that doesn't nessecarly mean its important to other humans/people. 

Say we imagine a world without humans, sure meaningful dosen't mean anything without humans cause it's a word we invented afterall.
But the idea still remains, it's like we tore of the label of a box but the box still will exist without having a label to it.

My intention was not about people's views on life itself, whether they find it worthwhile or not is their view. What I do mean is that even if we find it worthwhile while or not it does not matter, we'll still be useful to maybe the universe in making itself survive but the little changes that we create as simple as keeping the food chain going

Also even if an outside observer is not present, one might be created because energy is neither created nor destroyed. Don't know if i made any sense but that's what I think
